claim: Kernel backlight sysfs exposes /sys/class/backlight/<backlight>/brightness (R/W requested level), actual_brightness (RO, the level actually used by hardware) and max_brightness (RO).
stance_target: kiosk brightness control in ha-linux-agent has a stable, documented sysfs interface; actual_brightness is the authoritative readback because writes may be clamped by hardware
scope_conditions: Linux backlight core; requires a registered backlight device (driver support); full attribute list in the stable/sysfs-class-backlight ABI file
quoted_support: Several sysfs attributes are provided by the backlight core: - brightness R/W, set the requested brightness level - actual_brightness RO, the brightness level used by the HW - max_brightness RO, the maximum brightness level supported

claim: Backlight power state is configurable from user space via /sys/class/backlight/<backlight>/bl_power with values 0 (full on) and 4 (full off).
stance_target: agent can blank/restore kiosk displays via sysfs in addition to setting brightness
quoted_support: User space can configure the power mode using the sysfs attribute: /sys/class/backlight/<backlight>/bl_power ... The possible values are: (0: full on, 4: full off)

claim: Backlight changes are reported to user space via a uevent on the actual_brightness attribute, and when brightness is changed by platform means (e.g. a hotkey) the driver must call backlight_force_update() to notify the core and generate that uevent — so uevents (not polling) are the event-driven way to track external brightness changes.
stance_target: agent brightness state can stay in sync with hotkey/firmware changes by listening for uevents instead of polling sysfs
scope_conditions: Linux backlight core; well-behaved backlight drivers
quoted_support: When the backlight changes this is reported to user-space using an uevent connected to the actual_brightness attribute. When brightness is set by platform specific means, for example a hot-key to adjust backlight, the driver must notify the backlight core that brightness has changed using backlight_force_update().

claim: Backlight devices are typed RAW (hardware registers), PLATFORM (platform-specific interface) or FIRMWARE (standard firmware interface), and user space can use the type to make policy decisions about which interface to prefer.
stance_target: agent must enumerate and prefer backlight devices by type rather than assuming a single /sys/class/backlight entry, since a host can expose multiple backlight interfaces
quoted_support: The type of backlight control ... BACKLIGHT_RAW The backlight is controlled using hardware registers. BACKLIGHT_PLATFORM The backlight is controlled using a platform-specific interface. BACKLIGHT_FIRMWARE The backlight is controlled using a standard firmware interface. ... The backlight type allows userspace to make appropriate policy decisions based on the backlight type.
